shortlist.validation: Validation weak/negative (failed MEDI7247 ADC, no expression-response; only chemical probes are reversible uM amino-acid mimetics). Modality: oral covalent small molecule vs ADC + weak reversible probes.
shortlist.thesis: Cys467 is a quasi-catalytic substrate-pocket cysteine (C467A raises Gln Km ~10x) that the nearest paralogs (SLC1A4 Thr, EAATs Arg) lack, so a covalent warhead is intrinsically paralog-selective and gives washout-resistant transport blockade reversible competitors cannot achieve against high intracellular glutamine — genuine open white space, capped by unproven human target validation.

shortlist.validation: Seladelpar (PPARd agonist) FDA-approved 2024 validates the receptor, but for the OPPOSITE pharmacology (agonism/liver); the oncology antagonism thesis is clinically unproven. Modality: oral covalent inverse-agonist small molecule.
shortlist.thesis: Cys249 in LBD helix 3 is a structurally de-risked, selective covalent handle (proven by tool compound GSK3787) homologous to the heavily-drugged PPARG Cys313, so the validated PPARG covalent inverse-agonist playbook (Flare FX-909) can be ported to lock PPARD in a corepressor state for oncology — mechanism proven at tool-compound level but no drug-like clinical program exists.

shortlist.validation: Strong genetic validation (PKC-theta KO resistant to autoimmunity/GvHD while sparing antiviral/GvL); no approved selective drug, and a sophisticated reversible incumbent (EXS4318/BMS-986449) was deprioritized by BMS at Phase 1. Modality: oral covalent immunology small molecule.
shortlist.thesis: Cys424 sits where most kinases carry a His in the catalytic/HRD region — an isoform-distinguishing, active-site-proximal cysteine that could finally deliver the PKC-isoform selectivity that sank pan-PKC agents (sotrastaurin), giving durable T-cell-restricted immunosuppression; covalent space is open but warhead druggability of Cys424 is unconfirmed.

shortlist.validation: Decades-deep modern-small-molecule target concept but a graveyard of late-stage failures (AT-001 endpoint miss; govorestat CRL); no FDA-approved drug. Modality: oral covalent small molecule vs reversible ARIs.
shortlist.thesis: Cys298 is a highly nucleophilic active-site-adjacent cysteine that physiologically governs both catalysis and inhibitor sensitivity (C298S raises sorbinil Ki ~10x), with direct family precedent for warhead capture (PGA1 at AKR1B10 Cys299), so covalent durability could overcome the low-potency/PK failure mode of reversible ARIs — but AKR1B1>AKR1B10 selectivity and the fact that failures were efficacy/translation (not potency) cap conviction.

shortlist.validation: Modern targeted validation (dasatinib/bosutinib repurposed; CH6953755, NXP900 Phase 1b) but YES1 as a standalone driver is still emerging; no YES1-specific approval. Modality: oral covalent SFK inhibitor.
shortlist.thesis: YES1 is one of only 3 SRC-family kinases bearing a P-loop cysteine (Cys277, nM-validated covalently by Taunton-lab probes) giving a rare selectivity handle vs ~500 kinases and durable occupancy at low exposure for YES1-amplified NSCLC/SCLC/TNBC — but C277 is shared with SRC/FGR (no intra-SFK selectivity from warhead alone) and a differentiated reversible incumbent (NXP900) is already in Phase 1b.

shortlist.validation: Cleanest validation is genetic (SCA14 gain-of-function PKC-gamma) — a rare orphan CNS indication; oncology PKC pharmacology is a failure trail. Modality: brain-penetrant covalent small molecule (hard).
shortlist.thesis: Covalent capture of a gamma-unique cysteine is the literature-nominated way to break the conserved-ATP-pocket problem that defeated every reversible PKC program, and the covalent space is open — but the linchpin (a specific, ligandable, gamma-UNIQUE cysteine) is unconfirmed by primary structural/chemoproteomic data, making this the most contingent lane.

dead_existing_covalent: PDE3B — GSK (with 23andMe): reversible-covalent boronate at His737 (GSK4394835A, ~300x PDE3B-selective; His-directed, not Cys)
NR3C1 (GR) — UAntwerp/UAMC: covalent SEGRAs UAMC-1217/1218 at Cys622 (plus legacy dexamethasone-21-mesylate)
CPT1A — academic (Lou et al., Redox Biol 2023): DHP-B alpha-methylene-gamma-butyrolactone at Cys96 (plus legacy covalent etomoxir)
RXRA — Xiamen/Sanford-Burnham nitrostyrenes at Cys432 + K-80003 series; Flare Therapeutics FX-909 covalent (Phase 1) targets the PPARG heterodimer partner
PRKCI (PKC-iota) — auranofin/aurothiomalate: covalent thio-gold adduct at Cys69 (taken into Phase 1/feasibility cancer trials)
PDK1 (pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase) — JX06: covalent disulfide at Cys240 (IC50 ~49 nM, published structure/mechanism)
HDAC2 — YSR734 (J Med Chem 2023): covalent pentafluorobenzenesulfonamide at Cys274 (but Cys274 is conserved across HDAC1/2/3 — pan-Class-I, not selective)
AKR1C3 — RJG-2051 (J Med Chem 2025): SuTEx covalent inhibitor at non-catalytic Tyr24 (Tyr-directed, not Cys)
IDE — Durham group (ACS Chem Biol 2015): benzoisothiazolone forms reducible disulfide at Cys819 (quasi-irreversible, extracellular-only)

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: PDE3 is clinically validated, but only by OLD, non-selective PDE3 (PDE3A/PDE3B) small molecules: milrinone (IV inotrope, approved 1980s for decompensated heart failure), cilostazol/Pletal (intermittent claudication, also adenosine-uptake inhibitor), enoximone, amrinone/inamrinone. All are first-generation targeted small molecules (not cytotoxic chemo, not biologics), but NONE is PDE3B-selective and none is approved for the metabolic indication (obesity/T2D/NASH) that motivates a PDE3B-selective drug. The cardiac effects/inotropy and pro-arrhythmic liability of these legacy drugs derive largely from PDE3A; chronic oral PDE3 inhibition (milrinone PROMISE trial) increased mortality. So clinical validation for a PDE3B-SELECTIVE thesis is indirect and weak — the approved drugs validate PDE3 catalysis generally, not the metabolic-disease, PDE3B-isoform-selective concept.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES — a covalent program already exists. GSK (with 23andMe) ran a 1.9-trillion-member DNA-encoded library screen and published boronic-acid-based PDE3B-selective inhibitors (Rowley et al., J Med Chem 2024, 67:2049; up to ~300-fold PDE3B-over-PDE3A selectivity), including GSK4394835A. A 2025 structural re-refinement by the Christianson lab (bioRxiv 2025.10.22.684020; J Med Chem 2025, DOI 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c03081; PDB 9YUD) proved GSK4394835A is a REVERSIBLE COVALENT inhibitor — the boronic acid forms a tetrahedral boronate anion covalently bonded to active-site His737. So the covalent-small-molecule space on PDE3B is already occupied (by a large pharma, GSK), and the validated covalent chemistry is HISTIDINE-directed boronate, not cysteine.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/unsupported for a cysteine-covalent thesis. The only structurally documented covalent mechanism on PDE3B targets an active-site HISTIDINE (His737) via a boronic-acid/boronate, not a cysteine. PDE3B's catalysis is metal-dependent (Zn2+/Mg2+, Gln988 for nucleotide recognition); there is no described catalytic cysteine. PDE3B does carry a non-catalytic active-site cysteine at the position homologous to a Tyr in PDE3A — interesting as a potential SELECTIVITY handle vs the 95%-identical cardiac PDE3A — but it is a substrate-pocket residue, not catalytic, and there is no published evidence that the 10 CysDB-ligandable cysteines confer selective, functional covalent inhibition. CysDB ligandability (chemoproteomic labeling) is not the same as a productive, selective covalent inhibition site. The mechanistically attractive covalent handle here is His, and GSK already owns it.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: The covalent BIC slot is effectively closed. (1) Incumbent: GSK already has reversible-covalent, PDE3B-selective (~300x) chemistry validated by crystallography (His737 boronate) — a covalent small-molecule program from a major pharma is the textbook "not open" signal. (2) The patent-radar "no recent covalent patent program" is misleading: the covalent nature was only proven in late-2025 re-refinement, but the underlying GSK boronic-acid composition-of-matter (Rowley 2024) predates and covers the chemotype. (3) The CysDB cysteine angle is not the path the field is using — the demonstrated, selective covalent strategy is His-directed, so a cysteine-covalent program would be re-deriving selectivity that GSK already achieved by a different (His) mechanism, with no evidence the Cys route works. (4) The one genuinely interesting differentiation — a PDE3B-unique active-site Cys absent in PDE3A — could in principle give isoform selectivity to avoid cardiac PDE3A liability, but this is speculative, unvalidated, and the affinities achieved so far are only high-nanomolar. (5) Indication risk: PDE3B-selective metabolic disease (obesity/T2D) is now competing against GLP-1/incretin standard of care, raising the commercial bar enormously. Net: no clear covalent BIC differentiation, an existing covalent incumbent, and a cysteine rationale that the structural biology does not support.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Strongly validated by MODERN targeted small molecules and steroids, not old cytotoxic chemo. Glucocorticoid agonist steroids (dexamethasone, prednisone) are small-molecule drugs used in millions. On the antagonist side: mifepristone/Korlym (steroidal GR antagonist, FDA-approved for Cushing's hyperglycemia) and, decisively, relacorilant (Lifyorli, Corcept) — a non-steroidal SELECTIVE GR antagonist that received FDA approval in combination with nab-paclitaxel for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (ROSELLA Ph3, OS benefit). Deep clinical pipeline of selective non-steroidal GR modulators: nenocorilant (Ph1b + nivolumab), dazucorilant (Ph3 ALS, DAZALS showed ~84% reduction in 1-yr death risk), miricorilant, and ORIC-101. Target validation is therefore strong and modern, not weak.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES — covalent small-molecule GR ligands already exist as published prior art, so this target is NOT open for a covalent first. (1) GSK866 covalent analogs UAMC-1217 and UAMC-1218: non-steroidal selective GR modulators (SEGRAs) bearing electrophilic Michael-acceptor warheads; covalent binding to GR-LBD Cys622 confirmed by mass spectrometry; explicitly developed for long-lasting (negligible off-rate) topical anti-inflammatory use — Chirumamilla et al., Front Immunol 2017;8:1324, and Bioorg Med Chem Lett 2016 (UAntwerp/UAMC, "Novel SEGRAs with a covalent warhead for long-lasting inhibition"). (2) Dexamethasone 21-mesylate, a classic covalent affinity label of GR (labels Cys656/Cys643 region). The patent-radar "no recent covalent patent" flag does not equal a clear field: an academic covalent SEGRA chemotype is already published and the cysteine has been validated covalently.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically plausible and already demonstrated. The GR ligand-binding domain contains several reactive/functional cysteines: Cys622 (solvent-exposed, the most reactive site, confirmed covalently modified by GSK866 warheads); Cys643 inside the steroid-binding pocket (C643R mutation raises Kd ~6-fold, i.e. functionally coupled to steroid binding); and Cys736 near the AF2 helix (Cys736-to-Ser reduces hormone binding). None is a catalytic cysteine (GR is a nuclear receptor, not an enzyme), but the LBD cysteines are functional/orthosteric-adjacent and covalent engagement giving prolonged, near-irreversible modulation has been proven by MS. So covalent tractability is real — but the chemical/IP space around it is already occupied, not virgin.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Weak-to-nonexistent BIC case for a covalent FIRST. The target is well validated but the non-covalent competitive field is dense and already at/near the FDA finish line (relacorilant approved; nenocorilant, dazucorilant, ORIC-101 in clinic) — a covalent newcomer would have to beat a deeply entrenched selective-antagonist franchise (Corcept) rather than enter open space. Worse, the covalent angle itself is not novel: covalent SEGRA chemotypes targeting GR Cys622 are already published (UAMC-1217/1218) and dexamethasone-mesylate covalent labeling is decades old, so the "covalent = differentiated" thesis is undermined. Covalent irreversible blockade of a nuclear hormone receptor that physiologically must cycle (HPA-axis regulation, broad endogenous cortisol signaling) also carries on-target safety risk (adrenal insufficiency / HPA disinhibition) that a tunable reversible antagonist avoids — the existing reversible programs were specifically engineered to limit HPA disinhibition. No clear selectivity, oral, resistance, or duration win that a covalent molecule would uniquely capture here.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Strong, MODERN targeted-small-molecule validation (not old cytotoxic chemo): Belumosudil (Rezurock), an oral ROCK2-selective inhibitor, FDA-approved 2021 for chronic GVHD after >=2 prior lines (ORR ~75%) - the marquee ROCK2 validation. Broader ROCK class validated by approved reversible ATP-competitive small molecules: fasudil (Japan 1995, cerebral vasospasm), ripasudil (2014, glaucoma), netarsudil (2017, glaucoma). Active clinical ROCK2-selective pipeline: GV101 (Graviton, fibrosis/CNS/obesity; Sanofi-backed), zelasudil/RXC007 (Redx, Ph2a complete), TDI01 (IPF). All are TARGETED small molecules - validation quality is high. No biologic competes here. Modality of every validating agent = reversible ATP-competitive small molecule.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. Direct searches ("ROCK2 covalent inhibitor", acrylamide/irreversible ROCK programs, covalent-cysteine ROCK patents) surfaced NO covalent small-molecule program or drug. Every approved and clinical ROCK2 agent (belumosudil, GV101, zelasudil/RXC007, TDI01, fasudil/ripasudil/netarsudil) is reversible and ATP-competitive. Consistent with the patent radar's "no covalent program." Notably, a P-loop covalent-cysteine selectivity strategy has been demonstrated for the related kinase LIMK1 - but NOT for ROCK.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak / unconvincing. The drugged, validated pocket is the ATP site, and ROCK1 vs ROCK2 share 92% kinase-domain identity with ATP-binding regions described as "almost identical." There is NO well-characterized catalytic or proximal targetable cysteine in the ROCK2 ATP pocket analogous to KRAS-G12C, BTK-Cys481, or EGFR-Cys797. Reported ROCK2 isoform selectivity is driven by reversible contacts with non-conserved ASPARTATE residues (Asp176/Asp218), not a cysteine. The 5 CysDB-ligandable cysteines are not established as catalytic, allosteric, or as a selectivity handle. Critically, ROCK2-over-ROCK1 selectivity is the ENTIRE value driver, and reversible chemistry already achieves >100-1000x selectivity (GV101, zelasudil), so a covalent warhead in the near-identical ATP pocket adds little and risks cross-reacting with ROCK1.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent ROCK2 inhibitor has no clear path to beat incumbents. (1) Selectivity - the supposed BIC axis (ROCK2 vs ROCK1) is already solved by reversible inhibitors via non-cysteine determinants; the 92%-identical, near-identical ATP pockets mean a covalent warhead is more likely to hit ROCK1 too, undercutting the only differentiation that matters. (2) Duration/oral - belumosudil and the clinical ROCK2 selectives are already convenient oral agents; covalency offers marginal PK/duration benefit and adds idiosyncratic-tox and warhead-liability risk in chronic fibrotic/autoimmune indications where safety margins matter. (3) Resistance is not a driver here (non-oncogene, chronic fibrosis/immune indications), removing the classic covalent rationale. (4) No validated functional cysteine = no mechanistic anchor. The crowded, well-validated reversible field (belumosudil approved; Graviton/Sanofi, Redx, TDI01 advancing) plus absence of a tractable selectivity-conferring cysteine makes the covalent BIC case unpersuasive. The "open patent space" is most plausibly explained by the absence of an attractive covalent site, not a missed opportunity.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: All validating agents are reversible, non-covalent SMALL MOLECULES (carboxylic-acid/hydantoin/succinimide aldose reductase inhibitors), not cytotoxic chemo and not biologics. Marketed: epalrestat (approved Japan/India/China for diabetic peripheral neuropathy; NOT FDA-approved). Clinical-stage modern programs: AT-001/caficrestat (Applied Therapeutics, Phase 3 ARISE-HF in diabetic cardiomyopathy) and govorestat/AT-007 (CNS-penetrant ARI for classic galactosemia/SORD/PMM2-CDG). Historical: sorbinil, tolrestat, ranirestat, fidarestat, zopolrestat, ponalrestat (most failed or withdrawn for PK/efficacy/tox). IMPORTANT CAVEAT on the 'FDA-validated' premise: there is NO FDA-approved AKR1B1 drug. AT-001 ARISE-HF MISSED its primary endpoint (Jan 2024; only a non-SGLT2/GLP-1 subgroup hit p=0.040), and govorestat received an FDA Complete Response Letter (Nov 2024) for galactosemia. So validation is a decades-deep, modern-small-molecule target CONCEPT with a graveyard of late-stage clinical failures, not a clean approval.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: No covalent small-molecule DRUG or disclosed clinical/biotech program found for AKR1B1 ('AKR1B1 covalent inhibitor' returns no drug program; all clinical ARIs are reversible). The only covalent modifier on record is prostaglandin A1 (PGA1), an endogenous cyclopentenone prostaglandin that covalently adducts the active-site cysteine (selectively Cys299 in the paralog AKR1B10) — a chemical-biology tool/endogenous ligand, NOT a drug. Note adjacent precedent in the family: a SuTEx covalent AKR1C3 inhibitor (RJG-2051) engages a noncatalytic Tyr, showing covalent AKR targeting is feasible. Net: the covalent-drug space on AKR1B1 appears genuinely OPEN.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Strong. Cys298 is a highly nucleophilic residue adjacent to the active site and is a documented site of physiological covalent modification: S-glutathiolation by GSSG inactivates the enzyme; it is also modified by HNE, NO (S-nitrosylation), and acrolein, and is protected by bound NADPH. Most compelling for a selectivity thesis: C298S site-directed mutagenesis shifts Km/kcat 4-5x AND raises the Ki for the inhibitor sorbinil ~10-fold, i.e. Cys298 directly governs inhibitor binding/sensitivity, not just catalysis. The homologous Cys299 in AKR1B10 is covalently engaged by PGA1 and its mutation abolishes adduct formation — direct family precedent for warhead capture at this exact cysteine. Caveats: modification can be reversible (retro-Michael with GSH) and adduct-size-dependent (small electrophiles can ACTIVATE the enzyme while bulky lipids inactivate it), so warhead choice is non-trivial.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent inhibitor anchored to Cys298 is mechanistically attractive: it could deliver durable, near-irreversible target occupancy and high affinity at a cysteine that physiologically controls both activity and inhibitor sensitivity — potentially overcoming the low in-vivo potency/PK that sank reversible ARIs (the recurring failure mode of tolrestat/sorbinil/zopolrestat). Modality is right (small molecule, oral; field already has oral reversible drugs), and the covalent-drug niche is unoccupied. BUT three real obstacles cap the thesis: (1) Selectivity within the family — Cys298 (AKR1B1) and Cys299 (AKR1B10) are homologous and the two enzymes are highly structurally similar, so a Cys-directed warhead may not discriminate AKR1B1 from AKR1B10 (the classic AR/AKR1B10 selectivity problem); a covalent strategy helps vs other AKRs but not necessarily vs the nearest paralog. (2) The decades of clinical failure are about disease biology/translation and efficacy (AT-001 endpoint miss, govorestat CRL), not insufficient potency — a better binder may not fix the clinical-benefit problem, which is the core BIC risk. (3) Reversibility/activation behavior of Cys298 demands careful warhead tuning. Differentiation is therefore real but conditional: best-in-class would need to pair covalent durability with a clean AKR1B1>AKR1B10 selectivity window and a disease indication where target engagement is known to translate (e.g. a tissue/PK-limited setting where prior reversible ARIs under-delivered).

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Strong MODERN TARGETED small-molecule validation. Three FDA-approved CDK4/6 inhibitors anchor the target: palbociclib (Ibrance, 2015), ribociclib (Kisqali), abemaciclib (Verzenio) — all reversible ATP-competitive small molecules for HR+/HER2- breast cancer (metastatic + adjuvant), a multi-billion-dollar class. This is NOT old cytotoxic chemo; it is best-in-class-era targeted SM validation. However, the clinical activity is driven primarily by CDK4 in HR+ breast cancer; CDK6 is the component responsible for the class's dose-limiting myelosuppression/neutropenia.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: A covalent CDK6 inhibitor has just been published (academic/preclinical): "Discovery of a highly effective covalent inhibitor of CDK6 for triple-negative breast cancer," Eur. J. Med. Chem., Jan 2026 (ScienceDirect S0223523426000103). Lead compound C32 is a palbociclib-core acrylamide that covalently engages a CDK6 cysteine (CDK6 IC50 = 13 nM; ~200x more potent than palbociclib in TNBC cells). No company/clinical covalent CDK6 program identified, and consistent with the patent radar showing no recent covalent patent — but a validated covalent chemotype is now in the public literature. Separately, covalent CDK precedent exists for CDK7 (THZ1, Cys312) and CDK2, confirming the family is covalently tractable.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically tractable but NON-catalytic. CDK6 carries a ligandable cysteine reachable from an ATP-competitive scaffold (the C32 acrylamide off the palbociclib core engages it in/near the ATP pocket). It is not a catalytic residue and not an allosteric switch; it is an ATP-pocket cysteine used to convert a reversible binder into an irreversible one. Covalent engagement could in principle deliver CDK6-vs-CDK4 selectivity IF the cysteine is CDK6-unique (CDK4/6 are highly homologous, so this must be verified structurally). So the chemistry works — but selectively and irreversibly silencing CDK6 is the wrong biological goal.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: The covalent CDK6 thesis is biologically backwards and lacks a differentiation rationale. (1) The field is deliberately moving AWAY from CDK6: Pfizer's atirmociclib (PF-07220060), a CDK4-SELECTIVE reversible inhibitor, is in Phase 3 precisely to spare CDK6 and reduce neutropenia, because CDK6 (not CDK4) is essential for hematopoiesis/myeloid and erythroid development. (2) A potent, irreversible, long-duration covalent CDK6 inhibitor would MAXIMIZE the exact on-target myelosuppression that defines the class's dose-limiting toxicity — durability of target engagement is a liability here, not an asset. (3) The validated unmet need (post-CDK4/6i resistance, cleaner therapeutic index) is being addressed by CDK4-selective agents and CDK4/6 degraders, not by harder CDK6 inhibition. (4) An academic covalent CDK6 chemotype (C32) already demonstrates the approach in TNBC, eroding novelty even though it is unpatented. Net: validated target and a tractable cysteine, but no credible best-in-class covalent CDK6 story — selectivity/resistance/oral/duration arguments all point toward CDK4-selective, not covalent CDK6.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Seladelpar (Livdelzi), a selective PPARdelta AGONIST, received FDA accelerated approval Aug 2024 for primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) - a modern targeted small molecule (strong modality validation, NOT old cytotoxic chemo). GW501516/GW0742 are potent PPARdelta agonists but only preclinical (GW501516 abandoned for carcinogenicity). CRITICAL CAVEAT: all clinical validation is for AGONISM in metabolic/cholestatic liver disease. The covalent thesis would instead pursue PPARD ANTAGONISM/inverse-agonism in ONCOLOGY (PPARD is a validated pro-tumorigenic driver in colorectal and other cancers per multiple studies), which is a different, clinically-unproven therapeutic hypothesis from what seladelpar validates.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES - a covalent small molecule already exists on PPARD. GSK3787 is a well-characterized, potent (IC50 ~130 nM), SELECTIVE, IRREVERSIBLE COVALENT PPARbeta/delta antagonist that forms a covalent thioether bond at Cys249 in helix 3 of the ligand-binding domain (no PPARalpha affinity, only weak PPARgamma activity). It is, however, a RESEARCH TOOL COMPOUND, not a clinical drug or named drug program - no clinical development. No clinical-stage covalent PPARD inhibitor program was found in searches. Paralog precedent is heavy: PPARgamma covalent modifiers T0070907 (Cys313), BAY-4931/BAY-0069, and FX-909 (covalent inverse agonist, Phase 1 in bladder cancer).
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Excellent and structurally de-risked. Cys249 sits in helix 3 of the PPARD LBD - a ligandable, covalently addressable, functional/orthosteric cysteine proven by GSK3787 (Cys249 thioether adduct, selective over other PPARs). It is conserved with the analogous, heavily-drugged Cys313 of PPARgamma, where covalent ligands (T0070907, FX-909) flip the receptor into a corepressor-bound (NCOR) repressive state - i.e. covalent INVERSE agonism. This is among the best-validated covalent cysteines in the nuclear-receptor family, enabling selective covalent inhibition/repression.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Mechanistically the covalent angle is genuinely attractive: Cys249 covalent inverse-agonism could lock PPARD in a repressive, corepressor-recruiting state for ORAL oncology use (colorectal/other PPARD-driven tumors), with durability and selectivity advantages of irreversible engagement - directly analogous to Bayer/Flare's PPARgamma FX-909 inverse-agonist playbook now in Phase 1. BUT the 'no covalent program' premise is only half-true: GSK3787 already demonstrates selective PPARD covalent antagonism at Cys249, so the mechanism is NOT open white space - it is proven prior art at tool-compound level. The real (narrower) opportunity is that no one has converted this into a drug-like clinical program, and the validated PPARgamma covalent inverse-agonist strategy has not yet been ported to PPARD oncology. Two further cautions: (a) clinical validation is for the OPPOSITE pharmacology (agonism, liver) not antagonism/oncology; (b) chronic systemic PPARD inverse-agonism carries metabolic/safety unknowns. Net: a credible but crowded-mechanism, indication-unvalidated thesis.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Bexarotene (Targretin), FDA-approved 1999 for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL), is the validating drug. MODALITY: it is a MODERN, RXR-SELECTIVE targeted small molecule (a "rexinoid"), NOT old cytotoxic chemo — a genuine point in favor of target validation. However, two major caveats undercut a covalent-inhibitor BIC thesis: (a) bexarotene is a pan-RXR AGONIST that binds RXRalpha/beta/gamma with equivalent affinity — it validates RXR ACTIVATION, not inhibition, and is not RXRB-selective; (b) no RXRB-selective drug of any modality is approved. The validated therapeutic mechanism for this target is agonism (driving RXR homodimerization, apoptosis, differentiation), the opposite of what a covalent inhibitor would do. Reagent/tool RXR antagonists exist (UVI3003, danthron/rhein) but none are clinically validated.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: No covalent small-molecule INHIBITOR program or drug found for RXRB ("RXRB covalent inhibitor" returns nothing target-specific) — consistent with the patent radar. BUT covalent RXR chemistry is well-precedented in the literature and is occupied by AGONISM, not inhibition: organotins (tributyltin/TBT, triphenyltin) form a covalent Sn–S bond to Cys432 in helix H11 of the RXRalpha LBD (PDB 3E94, 1.9 A), and these act as potent AGONISTS/endocrine disruptors that stabilize the active AF-2 conformation. So the covalent-cysteine mechanism on RXR is mechanistically known and produces activation, undermining a covalent-inhibitor differentiation story.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically interesting but pointed the wrong way. The functional pocket cysteine is Cys432 (RXRalpha numbering), in helix H11 within the AF-2/ligand-binding region — RXR's H11 is uniquely broken at Cys432, forming an isolated hydrophobic sub-pocket. It is demonstrably covalently ligandable (organotins covalently attach there, accounting for their high affinity despite only partly filling the pocket). However, the proven consequence of covalently engaging Cys432 is receptor ACTIVATION (agonism), not inhibition — covalent occupancy stabilizes the active conformation. Conservation of this exact cysteine in RXRB (vs RXRalpha) was not explicitly confirmed by search, and the CysDB "2 ligandable cysteines" may include structural/zinc-finger cysteines rather than a pocket cysteine usable for selective inhibition. Net: a functional cysteine exists, but it is an agonism-coupled site, not an obvious selective-inhibition handle.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent small molecule is unlikely to beat existing drugs here as an INHIBITOR. (1) Wrong mechanism: clinical validation (bexarotene) and the only proven covalent event on the functional Cys432 both produce AGONISM; there is no disease where RXRB INHIBITION is the validated intervention. (2) No isoform target product profile: RXRB-selective biology is poorly defined therapeutically (its clearest distinct role is cell-surface localization on tumor macrophages — a delivery/targeting angle, not an inhibition angle), and RXR isoform cross-reactivity is exactly what drives bexarotene's dose-limiting hypothyroidism/hyperlipidemia, so selectivity is the known hard problem. (3) Differentiation is unclear: a covalent agonist would compete with a 25-year-generic (bexarotene) and next-gen non-covalent rexinoids already in development, with no evident selectivity/oral/duration advantage that covalency uniquely confers. The one defensible covalent angle (irreversible engagement of Cys432 for durable, isoform-selective modulation) is speculative and unvalidated, and would still face the agonist-vs-inhibitor mechanism mismatch. Skeptical default applies.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: PTK2B/PYK2 is validated clinically only as the SECONDARY paralog target of dual FAK/PYK2 inhibitors — never as a standalone driver. Defactinib (VS-6063), an oral reversible ATP-competitive dual FAK/PYK2 inhibitor, received its FIRST FDA approval in May 2025 in combination with avutometinib (a RAF/MEK clamp) for KRAS-mutant recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer (RAMP-201/ENGOT-OV60). Modality = modern targeted small molecule (NOT old cytotoxic chemo, NOT biologic), which is favorable on its face. BUT the efficacy-driving target is FAK (PTK2), with PYK2 co-inhibited as a close paralog; the combination rationale is FAK-mediated adaptive resistance to MEK blockade, not PYK2 biology. Other agents (PF-562271, VS-4718, CT-707/contefatinib, SJP1602) are all reversible ATP-competitive and FAK-primary. No approved or clinical drug validates PYK2 as the causal target. In Alzheimer's, PTK2B is a GWAS risk locus but genetics suggest inhibiting Pyk2 may WORSEN tau pathology — undermining a CNS rationale.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. Extensive web search ("PTK2B/PYK2 covalent inhibitor", warhead/Cys patent searches, chemoproteomics) surfaced no covalent small-molecule program, drug, or patent on PYK2. All known PYK2 chemical matter (defactinib, PF-562271, VS-4718, CT-707, SJP1602) is reversible/ATP-competitive. The covalent niche is technically unoccupied — consistent with the patent radar showing no covalent program.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/unproven. CysDB lists 2 ligandable cysteines, but ligandable in a global proteomic screen does NOT mean catalytic, allosteric, or active-site-positioned for selective inhibition. No catalytic cysteine in the PYK2 ATP pocket is reported, and no covalent chemoproteomic or warhead study targeting a functional PYK2 cysteine surfaced. Critically, FAK and PYK2 are close paralogs with highly conserved ATP sites; the published selectivity literature shows FAK-vs-PYK2 discrimination is achieved KINETICALLY via DFG/αC/P-loop conformational differences, not via a unique cysteine. There is no evidence either ligandable Cys gives functional, paralog-selective covalent inhibition. Covalent mechanistic attractiveness is therefore speculative, not established.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Thin. The favorable elements: modern targeted-SM validation (defactinib approval, May 2025) and a genuinely empty covalent space. But the BIC case fails the core tests: (1) PYK2 is a passenger paralog of FAK in every validated context — there is no indication where PYK2 (not FAK) is the proven efficacy driver, so a PYK2-selective covalent drug lacks a clear differentiated thesis; (2) the standalone-PYK2 biology (osteoporosis, inflammation, CNS) is preclinical and, in Alzheimer's, points toward inhibition being harmful; (3) covalent selectivity would have to be carved against a near-identical FAK active site with no demonstrated unique/functional cysteine — the one structural angle that could justify covalency is unsupported. A covalent FAK-family agent might offer durability/oral advantages, but FAK itself (not PYK2) is the validated node, and reversible dual inhibitors already occupy the clinic. No compelling reason a covalent PYK2-selective molecule beats the incumbents.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No FDA-approved small molecule. Strongest clinical validation is a BIOLOGIC and it FAILED: MEDI7247 (AstraZeneca/MedImmune), an anti-ASCT2 PBD antibody-drug conjugate, reached Phase 1 in relapsed/refractory heme malignancies (AML/MM/DLBCL; NCT03106428) and solid tumors but was discontinued — only 16.4% (11/67) response, dose-limiting thrombocytopenia/neutropenia, no MTD established, and crucially NO correlation between ASCT2 expression and response. Cetuximab (approved anti-EGFR mAb) only co-targets ASCT2 indirectly/incidentally. ASCA101 is in a Phase 2 cachexia trial (NCT07168226, starting ~late 2025) — unproven. All small-molecule inhibitors (V-9302, C118P/Sanhome, AHPC hydroxyprolines, Lc-BPE, aminobutanoic acids) are PRECLINICAL, reversible amino-acid mimetics; V-9302 is also non-specific (hits SNAT2/LAT1). So clinical validation = one failed biologic + non-specific chemical probes. No targeted small molecule has validated the mechanism in humans.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. No covalent / irreversible / electrophilic ASCT2 (SLC1A5) small-molecule program appears in the literature or patents (searches for "SLC1A5 covalent inhibitor" / "ASCT2 irreversible/electrophile" returned only reversible amino-acid-scaffold inhibitors). The covalent chemical space on Cys467 is open. (Only thiol-reactive lab reagents like MTS/methyl-Hg are documented, as mechanistic probes, not drugs.)
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Strong and mechanism-based. Cys467 sits directly in the substrate-binding pocket: structure/function work (Scalise/Indiveri; cryo-EM, eLife 2019) shows it is positioned to donate a proton to the glutamine carbonyl, is a determinant of substrate selectivity and of the antiport mechanism, and C467A raises the Km for glutamine ~10-fold (i.e. it is functionally near-essential for transport). It is redox-sensitive and is directly inhibited by thiol-modifying reagents (methyl-Hg, MTS), demonstrating it is solvent-accessible and reactive. This is close to a quasi-catalytic/functional cysteine — exactly the kind of handle where covalent occupancy should durably abolish transport. Selectivity bonus: the paralog SLC1A4/ASCT1 has Thr (Thr459), not Cys, at the equivalent position, and EAAT glutamate transporters carry Arg there — so a covalent warhead targeting Cys467 is intrinsically paralog-discriminating. Caveat: Cys467 is buried in a multi-conformational membrane-transporter pocket, so warhead reach is conformation-dependent and engineering accessible reactivity into a membrane-permeant amino-acid-like scaffold is non-trivial.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent small molecule has a credible BIC path here, but on a target of unproven human relevance. The white space is real: every existing ASCT2 ligand is a reversible, low-affinity (often µM, e.g. V-9302 IC50 ~9.6 µM), poorly selective amino-acid mimetic, and the only clinical agents are a failed ADC (MEDI7247) and an early cachexia asset. Covalent targeting of Cys467 — a functional, substrate-pocket, redox-active cysteine absent in the closest paralogs — could deliver the selectivity and durable, washout-resistant transport blockade that reversible competitive ligands cannot (they fight high intracellular/plasma glutamine), enabling lower/intermittent oral dosing. That is a genuine differentiation thesis vs. an ADC (which carries the PBD payload's hematologic toxicity and antigen-density problems) and vs. weak reversible probes. BUT the BIC case is undercut by target validation: MEDI7247 showed minimal efficacy AND no expression-response relationship, V-9302's phenotypes are partly off-target, and glutamine-uptake redundancy (SNAT/LAT family) plus normal-tissue ASCT2 expression raise therapeutic-window and on-target-toxicity concerns. So: covalently tractable and chemically open, but the clinical-validation pillar is weak/negative, which caps conviction.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: VDR is validated clinically almost entirely by AGONISTS, not inhibitors. Approved drugs are vitamin D analogs acting as selective VDR activators: calcitriol, paricalcitol (19-nor-1,25-(OH)2-D2, FDA-approved for secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD), doxercalciferol, alfacalcidol, falecalcitriol, eldecalcitol (osteoporosis), and calcipotriol/calcipotriene (topical psoriasis). MODALITY = modern targeted small molecules (selective nuclear-receptor modulators), NOT cytotoxic chemo and not biologics. In oncology, the AGONIST paricalcitol has been trialed in metastatic pancreatic cancer (stroma/tumor-microenvironment modulation, +/- gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel or pembrolizumab) with negative-to-mixed results. Critically, there is NO approved VDR antagonist/inhibitor — so the validated pharmacology is agonism, which is the wrong direction for a covalent inhibitor thesis.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES — covalent VDR space is already well-trodden, contradicting the "no covalent program" radar flag. (1) TEI-9647 (Teijin) is a covalent VDR ANTAGONIST: its 25-dehydro-lactone exo-methylene acts as a Michael acceptor that alkylates the CysDB cysteines C403/C410, with H395 positioning the warhead (multiple J Med Chem / SAR papers, 2004-2015). (2) Electrophilic vitamin D analogs were designed as covalent VDR modifiers targeting His301/His305 (JMC 2018, 'Identification of the Histidine Residue in VDR That Covalently Binds Electrophilic Ligands'). (3) MeTC7 (Univ. of Rochester, Wilmot Cancer Institute) is a recent VDR antagonist bearing a bromoacetoxy alkylating warhead; a dedicated 2025 J Med Chem paper ('Mechanism of Inhibition of the MeTC7 Ligand That Covalently Binds to VDR to Reduce PD-L1 Expression', doi 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c02589) explicitly establishes covalent binding in the canonical ligand-binding pocket. The covalent-cysteine (C403/C410) antagonist concept is decades old and academically validated. Programs are academic/legacy-pharma, none commercially advancing — but the chemical space is occupied, not open.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically weak/mixed. VDR is a ligand-activated transcription factor with NO catalytic cysteine. The two CysDB-ligandable cysteines are C403/C410, located near helix-12/AF-2 at the rim of the ligand-binding domain. They are FUNCTIONAL only for ANTAGONISM — covalent alkylation there locks out the agonist (active AF-2) conformation; this is exactly how TEI-9647 works. They are not allosteric handles for the validated agonist pharmacology. Two further liabilities: (i) species divergence — TEI-9647 is antagonistic on human VDR but agonistic on rat VDR because of C-terminal/cysteine context differences, complicating preclinical translation; (ii) residual agonism is a recurring problem with VDR antagonists. So the cysteine is selective-enough to enable covalent antagonism but does not unlock a differentiated mechanism beyond what TEI-9647/MeTC7 already demonstrate.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Weak. A covalent small molecule does not have a clear path to beat existing VDR drugs because the directions are mismatched: the entire validated, approved franchise is AGONIST (CKD-MBD, osteoporosis, psoriasis) — those indications need activation, not covalent inactivation, and a covalent warhead on a nuclear-receptor LBD naturally produces antagonism. The only covalent-amenable thesis is VDR ANTAGONISM in oncology (VDR overexpression / PD-L1 / pancreatic-neuroblastoma-ovarian), but (a) this indication is unvalidated — the agonist paricalcitol itself underperformed in pancreatic-cancer trials, casting doubt on VDR as an oncology driver in either direction; (b) it is NOT open white space — Teijin's TEI-9647 covalent-cysteine series and Rochester's covalent MeTC7 already occupy it; (c) covalent VDR antagonists carry known species-divergence and residual-agonism liabilities. The patent radar's 'no recent covalent patent' most plausibly reflects commercial abandonment of a hard, poorly-validated antagonist target rather than untapped opportunity. No compelling selectivity/oral/resistance/duration edge presents itself over the established agonist analogs.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: STRONG, modern targeted small-molecule validation (not cytotoxic chemo). Four FDA-approved oral, ATP-competitive, reversible small-molecule JAK2 inhibitors anchor a large MPN/myelofibrosis franchise: ruxolitinib (2011, JAK1/2; also PV and GVHD; multi-billion-dollar drug), fedratinib (2019, selective JAK2), pacritinib (2022, JAK2/IRAK1/FLT3), momelotinib (2023, JAK1/2/ACVR1). Oncogenic driver is JAK2 V617F (about 90 percent of PV, roughly 50 to 60 percent of ET/MF). Gold-standard small-molecule target validation; no reliance on old cytotoxic chemo.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: No approved or clinical covalent JAK2 inhibitor (none clinical). But covalent JAK2 is a documented dead end, not white space: academic medchem (lysine-reactive pseudokinase series, Eur J Med Chem 2025) aimed acrylamide warheads at JH2 Cys675 (about 7.6 angstrom from pocket) and the productive adduct formed on Lys677 (a lysine), not the cysteine. All leading next-gen V617F mutant-selective programs are explicitly reversible/non-covalent: Ajax/Lilly AJ1-11095 (Phase 1 type II), Prelude/Incyte JAK2V617F (IND first half 2026), Atavistik Bio (allosteric JH2, ASH 2025).
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: WEAK and mechanistically unfavorable. JAK2 lacks the productive active-site/allosteric cysteine that makes the other JAKs covalently tractable: JAK1 C817, TYK2 C838, JAK3 C909 are exploited for selective covalent inhibition, but the literature is explicit this cysteine is NOT present in JAK2 - which is precisely why selective covalent inhibitors exist for JAK1/JAK3/TYK2 and not JAK2. The CysDB-flagged JAK2 cysteines (e.g. Cys675) sit in the catalytically dead JH2 pseudokinase domain, not the ATP catalytic site; there is no catalytic cysteine. Cys675 is near the V617F allosteric pocket but proved non-productive (covalent capture defaulted to adjacent Lys677). Neither catalytic nor reliably ligandable as a cysteine.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent small molecule is NOT the right wedge for JAK2. The real unmet need (durable disease modification and mutant selectivity sparing wild-type JAK2 to avoid anemia and thrombocytopenia) is already being solved by reversible mutant-selective JH2/type-II binders (Ajax, Prelude/Incyte, Atavistik, Lilly) that achieve over 100-fold V617F selectivity and clean profiles across over 300 kinases without a warhead. Covalency offers no clear selectivity or durability edge: JAK2 has no catalytic/allosteric cysteine to anchor selective irreversible binding, and the one nearby JH2 cysteine (C675) is a proven non-productive handle (adduct shifts to K677). Covalent JAK2 is a tried-and-abandoned approach; the absence of a recent covalent patent program reflects the field correctly walking away, not an overlooked opportunity. No credible covalent BIC thesis.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No PKC-theta-SELECTIVE drug is FDA-approved, so validation is partial/mechanistic rather than by an approved selective agent. (1) Midostaurin (FDA 2017, AML/advanced systemic mastocytosis) hits PRKCQ but is a pan-kinase staurosporine derivative whose approved mechanism is FLT3/KIT, not PKC-theta — incidental, weak validation. (2) The real target validation is modern and targeted-small-molecule: sotrastaurin/AEB071 (Novartis), a reversible pan-PKC inhibitor most potent on PKC-theta (Ki ~0.22 nM), reached Phase 2 in transplant rejection and psoriasis but was never approved and is non-selective. (3) Strong genetic validation: PKC-theta-knockout mice are resistant to Th2/Th17 autoimmunity, GvHD, and allograft rejection while sparing antiviral/graft-vs-leukemia immunity — the basis for I&I interest. So validation is "modern targeted SM + genetics," not old cytotoxic chemo, but no approved selective drug exists.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: No covalent PKC-theta program found in literature or patents. BUT a serious modern REVERSIBLE selective incumbent exists: EXS4318 / BMS-986449 (Exscientia, AI-designed, in-licensed by BMS Aug 2021), a selective PKC-theta inhibitor that reached Phase 1 (first-in-human 2023) for immunology/inflammation. Its structure and mechanism are undisclosed; a single low-quality AI search snippet labeled it "covalent," but no primary source (Wikipedia, Exscientia/BMS releases, patent IL307669A metadata) confirms covalency — it is described as binding the catalytic domain, consistent with a reversible ATP-site inhibitor. BMS appears to have deprioritized EXS4318 (~$40M/yr savings from 2025). Boehringer Ingelheim holds an older reversible (pyridine-derivative) PKC-theta patent estate, and WO2024025896 covers further (reversible) PKC-theta compounds. Net: no covalent incumbent confirmed; covalent chemical space appears open, but a well-funded reversible selective program already mapped the target.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically attractive. The PKC-theta catalytic-domain crystal structure (with staurosporine) identifies Cys424 sitting at a position where most kinases carry a histidine in the catalytic/HRD region — i.e., a non-conserved, active-site-proximal cysteine that distinguishes PKC-theta from related isoforms. The central reason pan-PKC drugs (sotrastaurin) failed was inability to selectively inhibit PKC-theta over ~9 closely related PKC isoforms; an isoform-unique active-site cysteine is exactly the handle that could deliver covalent isoform selectivity plus durable target occupancy. This is a genuine functional/selectivity cysteine, not a generic distal surface thiol — a real BIC differentiator if the geometry supports a warhead.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent PKC-theta inhibitor targeting the isoform-distinguishing active-site Cys424 could deliver what every prior program lacked: PKC-isoform selectivity. Pan-PKC reversible agents (sotrastaurin) failed on selectivity/tolerability; even the AI-designed selective reversible EXS4318/BMS-986449 reached only Phase 1 before BMS deprioritized it, showing selectivity+potency is genuinely hard reversibly. Covalent occupancy of Cys424 could lock in selectivity and give durable, T-cell-restricted immunosuppression (oral, autoimmune/I&I) sparing antiviral and graft-vs-leukemia immunity. Caveats keeping this out of STRONG: (a) no approved selective drug validates the mechanism in patients; (b) a sophisticated reversible selective incumbent already exists/existed and a deep-pocketed sponsor (BMS) walked back interest, signaling either commercial or biological risk; (c) irreversible covalent binding in chronic autoimmune indications raises the safety/idiosyncratic-toxicity bar; (d) Cys424 druggability with a warhead is unconfirmed in any covalent SAR. Compelling open covalent angle on a validated-by-genetics target, but not a clean lane.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No FDA-approved CPT1A-selective drug exists. Clinical validation is weak and largely OLD/non-oncology: perhexiline (CPT1/2 inhibitor, EMA-approved for angina, recalled in some markets for hepatotoxicity + peripheral neurotoxicity) and ranolazine (FDA/EMA-approved anti-anginal, acts on FAO pathway) are cardiovascular drugs, NOT cancer agents. Etomoxir (irreversible CPT1A inhibitor) failed Phase II for type-2 diabetes/heart failure due to hepatotoxicity. ST1326/teglicar reached Phase 2 (diabetes) and is a preclinical leukemia tool. In oncology, CPT1A is validated only PRECLINICALLY via non-selective tool compounds (etomoxir, teglicar) plus CRISPR/genetic knockout across CRC, TNBC, ovarian, glioblastoma, leukemia, NPC. Modality of validation = old cytotoxic/non-selective metabolic tool compounds and genetic studies; no modern targeted small molecule or biologic has clinically validated this target. This is the weak-validation pattern.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES - a covalent program already exists, so the target is NOT covalently open. (1) DHP-B (2,6-dihydroxypeperomin B): an explicitly characterized covalent CPT1A inhibitor that binds Cys96 via an alpha-methylene-gamma-butyrolactone warhead, confirmed by QTRP/MST/CETSA, with in vivo anti-colorectal-cancer activity and CPT1A-VDAC1 axis disruption (Lou et al., Redox Biology 2023, PMC10692921; academic, not yet a company program). (2) Etomoxir itself is a covalent/irreversible active-site inhibitor (alpha-epoxy carboxylate warhead) reported in the literature as a covalent inhibitor of the CPT1 active site. So both an academic targeted covalent inhibitor (DHP-B, defined warhead + defined Cys96) and a legacy covalent active-site agent already exist. The patent-radar "no recent covalent patent" flag is misleading: the covalent biology is published even if no recent composition-of-matter patent was captured.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Partial. Cys96 is a confirmed ligandable, FUNCTIONAL cysteine - C96A mutants are resistant to DHP-B (covalent engagement abolishes drug effect) - and engagement blocks FAO plus disrupts the CPT1A-VDAC1 protein interaction. However, Cys96 is NOT the documented catalytic residue: catalysis centers on His473 (acyl-CoA site) and Gly709/710, and malonyl-CoA binds the C-terminus. DHP-B's effect is thus allosteric/functional/PPI-disrupting rather than active-site catalytic. The deeper problem: CPT1A shares high homology with CPT1B (heart/muscle) and CPT1C (brain); every prior inhibitor (etomoxir, perhexiline, teglicar) suffered isoform cross-reactivity and on-/off-target cardiac, hepatic and neurotoxicity. Whether a covalent Cys96 binder can deliver clean CPT1A-vs-CPT1B/C selectivity is unproven and is the central risk.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent BIC case is hard to make and the lane is not clean. Arguments against: (a) a covalent inhibitor already exists at Cys96 with a defined warhead and in vivo efficacy (DHP-B), plus legacy covalent etomoxir - the covalent mechanism/site is published prior art, undermining freedom-to-operate and the "first covalent" differentiation; (b) clinical validation is old/non-selective cardiovascular drugs that were recalled or failed for hepatotoxicity/neurotoxicity, not a modern targeted-oncology win; (c) the historical failure mode is exactly the kind covalency does not automatically solve - isoform (CPT1B/C) cross-reactivity and mitochondrial/hepatic tox. A theoretical covalent BIC edge (durable Cys96 engagement -> sustained FAO blockade with lower/intermittent dosing, potentially below the tox threshold that killed etomoxir; oral) is conceivable but speculative and would have to out-engineer a known covalent scaffold while proving the selectivity that no prior CPT1 agent achieved. Net: the differentiation that would justify a covalent program is largely pre-empted and the safety thesis is unproven.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: RXRA (Retinoid X Receptor alpha, NR2B1) is a nuclear hormone receptor validated almost exclusively by AGONISTS, not inhibitors. Flagship: bexarotene (Targretin), an RXR-agonist rexinoid, FDA-approved 1999 for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; also alitretinoin (9-cis-retinoic acid) and isotretinoin act through RXR. These are modern, targeted small molecules (not old cytotoxic chemo), which is favorable for tractability. BUT the validating modality is AGONISM (activating transcription), studied in CTCL and explored in Alzheimer's/MS. This is a fundamental mechanistic mismatch for a covalent BIC thesis, since covalent small molecules are overwhelmingly inhibitors/antagonists/inverse agonists, not agonists.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES — the covalent space on RXRA is NOT open. (1) Nitrostyrene derivatives covalently engage RXRA's ligandable Cys432 (LBD) via Michael addition (Xiamen University / Sanford-Burnham; Cancer Res 2015, PMC4433622) — same cysteine our radar flags. (2) The K-80003 / sulindac-derived tRXRα antagonist series binds the same LBD pocket (Cys432-dependent) for cancer. (3) Most importantly, the clinically advanced covalent approach to RXRA-driven disease already exists as a Phase 1 drug: Flare Therapeutics' FX-909, a covalent PPARG inverse agonist for PPARG/RXRA-activated muscle-invasive urothelial cancer — it covalently targets the RXRA heterodimer partner (PPARG) rather than RXRA, and counters RXRA-induced conformational bias. So both the direct-covalent-on-Cys432 concept and the commercially differentiated covalent strategy are already taken.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Cys432 is genuinely functional/allosteric: it sits in the ligand-binding domain, and Cys432 mutation (to Trp/Tyr) causes autoactivation, indicating it gates the LBD conformation. It is engaged by nitrostyrenes (Michael adduct) and is part of the pocket exploited by tetramerization-inducing antagonists. So mechanistically it is a real functional cysteine. HOWEVER, the reported covalent engagement is weak, reversible, and microenvironment-sensitive (fast SPR off-rates, micromolar tool compounds; the authors explicitly could not confirm durable covalent binding). So it is functional but not a clean, high-occupancy covalent handle, and selectivity vs. RXRB/RXRG (highly conserved LBDs) is unaddressed.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: The BIC thesis is weak and largely foreclosed. (1) Modality mismatch: clinical validation is for AGONISM (bexarotene), whereas covalent chemistry naturally delivers inhibition/inverse-agonism — building a covalent antagonist where the validated, marketed mechanism is activation inverts the proven biology. (2) Not open: direct covalent engagement of the exact ligandable cysteine (Cys432) is already published (nitrostyrenes, K-80003 pocket), and the commercially serious covalent play on RXRA biology — Flare's FX-909 — is a Phase 1 covalent drug that targets the PPARG partner, capturing the differentiated angle. (3) The functional anti-tumor RXRA biology (tRXRα/PI3K, TNFα/NF-kB) is real but has been chased academically for a decade without a clinical covalent RXRA antagonist emerging, suggesting tractability/selectivity hurdles. A covalent small molecule does not obviously beat bexarotene (oral, approved) on its validated indication, and the inhibitor niche is crowded by prior covalent tool compounds plus a clinical partner-targeting covalent drug.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Strong, MODERN targeted small-molecule validation (not old cytotoxic chemo). Three FDA-approved COMT inhibitors, all rationally designed reversible competitive nitrocatechol substrate-mimics used as levodopa adjuncts for "wearing off" in Parkinson's disease: entacapone (Comtan), tolcapone (Tasmar; liver-tox limited), and opicapone (Ongentys, approved 2020, once-daily, extra-slow dissociation/very long duration). Active discovery pipelines (non-nitrocatechol classes e.g. LIBD-1/-3, baicalein/flavonoid derivatives) are also all reversible. Modality = modern targeted small molecule. Good for a validation argument, but the incumbents are strong.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. Web searches for "COMT covalent inhibitor," covalent/irreversible/acrylamide-warhead programs, and recent (2023-2025) biotech pipelines returned no covalent small-molecule COMT program or drug. All marketed drugs and all current discovery efforts are non-covalent reversible competitive inhibitors binding the catechol/SAM active site. The covalent modality appears nominally open.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/unattractive. COMT has NO catalytic cysteine — catalysis runs through Mg2+-coordinated catechol binding plus the SAM methyl-donor pocket (catalytic Lys is non-essential). The CysDB-ligandable cysteines (C95, C173, C188) are non-conserved, solvent-exposed surface residues implicated in disulfide/glutathione-adduct formation. Cys-95 IS functionally relevant in that its OXIDATION inactivates the enzyme (Ser-95 substitution protects from inactivation; DTT restores activity) — but this is redox-regulatory surface chemistry, not an orthosteric active-site cysteine. Engaging a solvent-exposed, redox-labile, non-conserved surface Cys raises serious GSH-competition and selectivity liabilities and offers no clear mechanistic handle for selective active-site inhibition.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Weak. Covalent's signature advantage — prolonged duration via long residence time — is ALREADY achieved non-covalently: opicapone is once-daily with extra-slow dissociation and tight, slow off-rate binding. The real unmet need is brain-penetrant CNS COMT inhibition for cognition, which a covalent acrylamide on a solvent-exposed surface cysteine does not obviously solve and which adds tox/selectivity risk (GSH scavenging, off-target labeling, idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity precedent already exists with tolcapone). There is no functional active-site cysteine to deliver selective covalent orthosteric inhibition, so a covalent program would target a redox-regulatory surface thiol with an unclear PK/PD and differentiation story versus an already-excellent reversible class. No compelling covalent BIC thesis.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Validation is MODERN TARGETED small molecule, not old cytotoxic chemo — favorable for a BIC thesis. (1) Dasatinib and bosutinib (FDA-approved SRC/ABL multikinase TKIs for Ph+ CML) are used off-label/preclinically as YES1 inhibitors; YES1 amplification predicts dasatinib sensitivity in lung cancer and TNBC, and YES1 status is being developed as a stratification biomarker (investigational, not an approved YES1 label). (2) Dedicated targeted agents: CH6953755 (Chugai, selective YES1 inhibitor, preclinical), NXP900 (Nuvectis SRC/YES1, Phase 1b, incl. combos with osimertinib/lorlatinib), and MRANK-106 (dual WEE1/YES1, FDA-cleared Phase 1). Caveat: no drug is approved specifically FOR YES1; YES1 as a standalone clinically validated driver is still emerging rather than fully established.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found as a drug/clinical program. The leading SRC/YES1 clinical asset, NXP900 (Nuvectis, Phase 1b), is explicitly a REVERSIBLE non-covalent 'type 1.5' conformational inhibitor (locks closed/autoinhibited conformation, blocks catalytic + scaffolding function) — not covalent. CH6953755 (Chugai) and dasatinib/bosutinib are reversible ATP-competitive. The only covalent YES1 work is ACADEMIC chemical-biology probes: vinylsulfonate/electrophilic inhibitors targeting the Src-family G-loop Cys277 (Taunton lab and follow-ups), which label endogenous YES1 at single-digit nM but are tool compounds, not drug programs. No dedicated covalent YES1 drug-discovery/patent program identified — covalent space appears OPEN.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Mechanistically attractive. YES1 is one of only ~9 human kinases — and just 3 of the 9 SRC-family kinases (SRC, YES, FGR) — that carry a cysteine at the tip of the glycine-rich P-loop/G-loop (Cys277 in Src numbering), positioned adjacent to the ATP pocket near catalytic Lys295. It is non-catalytic/allosteric, solvent-exposed, and ATP-site-proximal, and is academically validated as covalently ligandable (single-digit nM vinylsulfonate probes; C277S mutation abolishes covalent potency). This gives a genuine selectivity handle versus the ~500 kinases lacking the residue. IMPORTANT limitation: the cysteine is SHARED by SRC and FGR, so it does not by itself confer intra-SFK (YES1-vs-SRC) selectivity — that must come from the reversible recognition scaffold. CysDB's '1 ligandable cysteine' is consistent with this single exploitable C277.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Plausible POSSIBLE-BIC. Validation is targeted/modern (dasatinib, CH6953755, NXP900) rather than cytotoxic, the target has a well-characterized, structurally rare, covalently ligandable P-loop cysteine (C277) with literature precedent for nM covalent engagement, and no covalent drug program currently occupies the space. A covalent agent could deliver durable target occupancy and deeper pathway shutdown (kinase + scaffolding) at lower systemic exposure, potentially improving the therapeutic index over dasatinib (whose SFK-class toxicity has blocked solid-tumor use) and offering a resistance/duration edge in YES1-amplified NSCLC/SCLC/TNBC and as an ALK/EGFR-resistance combination agent. HEADWINDS that temper the case: (i) C277 is shared with SRC/FGR, so YES1-selectivity is not achievable from the warhead alone; (ii) a well-funded reversible incumbent (NXP900) with a differentiated dual catalytic+scaffolding MoA is already in Phase 1b, raising the differentiation bar; (iii) YES1's standalone driver biology is still emerging, and selective covalent SFK inhibition risks pan-SFK toxicity unless the reversible scaffold delivers selectivity. A covalent program is differentiated only if it pairs the C277 warhead with a YES1-biased reversible core and a clear ADMET/duration advantage over NXP900.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: Validation is for AMPK as a complex, not PRKAB2 specifically, and it is metabolic/activation-driven rather than oncology. Approved validation is dominated by metformin (old, INDIRECT AMPK activator - does not bind AMPK; raises AMP:ATP) plus salicylate/AICAR - i.e. weak, non-targeted, decades-old pharmacology. Modern DIRECT activators bind the allosteric ADaM site at the alpha-kinase/beta-CBM interface: Pfizer PF-06409577/PF-739, Merck MK-8722, Betagenon O304, Cambrian/Amplifier ATX-304 (Ph1b/2a obesity), SCYNEXIS SCY-770, and Nimbus/Lilly+Pfizer isoform-selective activators (~$500M Lilly deal). ALL are ACTIVATORS, all reversible allosteric small molecules, and the advanced/selective ones are beta1-selective or pan-AMPK (PF-06409577 is >5000x selective for beta1 over beta2). No approved or clinical drug selectively targets PRKAB2/beta2. Modality of validation: modern targeted small molecule, but aimed at activation and largely NOT at beta2.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: No covalent small-molecule inhibitor or activator specifically on PRKAB2/AMPKbeta2 found via web search ("PRKAB2 covalent inhibitor" returns nothing on-target). However the druggable site on the beta subunit (ADaM site) is already heavily prosecuted by multiple companies with REVERSIBLE allosteric activators (Pfizer, Merck, Nimbus/Lilly, Cambrian/Amplifier, Betagenon, SCYNEXIS). So the pocket is not virgin space - it is a crowded reversible-activator field. No covalent incumbent specifically, but no covalent program either because there is no thesis for covalently drugging this scaffolding subunit.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/absent. PRKAB2 encodes the beta2 NON-CATALYTIC regulatory/scaffolding subunit of AMPK - it has NO catalytic activity, so there is no catalytic cysteine to inactivate. The functionally important beta2 residues are threonines (Thr-148, Thr-101 in the carbohydrate-binding module governing glycogen binding), not a cysteine. The single CysDB-ligandable cysteine is not described as catalytic, and the ADaM allosteric site is engaged by reversible activators, not a covalent cysteine trap. Covalently labeling a surface cysteine on a scaffolding subunit has no validated functional consequence - you cannot "inhibit" a scaffold the way you inhibit an enzyme, and the therapeutically validated direction is ACTIVATION, not inhibition. No mechanistic basis for selective, functionally meaningful covalent engagement.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: A covalent small molecule has no clear path to beat existing drugs here. (1) Wrong protein class: PRKAB2 is a non-catalytic scaffolding subunit, not an enzyme - there is no catalytic/allosteric cysteine that, when covalently modified, produces the desired pharmacology. (2) Wrong direction: the validated AMPK thesis is ACTIVATION (metabolic disease, obesity, ADPKD), and the field already has potent reversible ADaM-site activators in the clinic; covalent inhibition of beta2 would be at best metabolically deactivating, which is not a validated or attractive indication, and beta2-selective inhibition (e.g. via MT47-100 chemistry) has no clinical rationale. (3) Crowded reversible field: even the activation thesis is occupied by Pfizer, Merck, Nimbus/Lilly, Cambrian/Amplifier, Betagenon, SCYNEXIS. (4) Selectivity hazard: beta2 differs from beta1 only modestly; pan-AMPK activation carries cardiac-hypertrophy safety concerns. There is no differentiation story (selectivity, oral, resistance, duration) that a covalent beta2 binder uniquely unlocks. The "FDA-validated target + no covalent patent" signal here is a false positive driven by AMPK-complex-level validation being mis-attributed to the beta2 scaffolding subunit.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: NONE that genuinely validate IDE clinically. After 60+ years, IDE (insulin-degrading enzyme; M16A zinc metalloprotease) has NO FDA-approved drug, no clinical-stage program, and no biotech pipeline. All inhibitors are preclinical/academic tools: BDM44768 (catalytic-site, Dabous/De Backer/Nature Comms 2015), 6bK macrocycle (Maianti/Liu, Nature 2014; >1000x selective, in vivo active), and substrate-selective non-active-site inhibitors (Saghatelian, Nat Chem Biol 2019). The 'FDA-validated target' premise is incorrect. The only marketed-drug link is incidental and off-target: carfilzomib (proteasome inhibitor) hits IDE as a non-proteasomal off-target — this does NOT validate IDE as a deliberate therapeutic target. So there is no validating modality at all, let alone modern targeted-SM validation.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: YES — a covalent program already exists in the literature. Cabrol et al./Durham group, 'Selective Targeting of Extracellular Insulin-Degrading Enzyme by Quasi-Irreversible Thiol-Modifying Inhibitors,' ACS Chem Biol 2015 (PMID 26398879): benzoisothiazolone covalent inhibitors with an isothiazolone warhead that undergoes ring-opening to form a disulfide with Cys819; lead IC50(app) ~63 nM, nontoxic to 100 uM. Earlier covalent thiol modifiers (e.g., cyanidin-3-O-glucoside) also reported. Covalent IDE inhibition is therefore published prior art, not an open white space. No covalent CLINICAL/commercial drug exists, but the chemical concept and Cys is already disclosed.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak. IDE is a ZINC metalloprotease — catalysis is zinc-dependent (HxxEH motif), not cysteine-dependent. The CysDB-ligandable/covalently-targeted cysteine is Cys819, which sits in the internal catalytic chamber but is NOT the catalytic nucleophile. Worse, the published covalent mechanism forms a DISULFIDE, which is reducible: it reverses under intracellular reducing conditions, so it only inhibits extracellular IDE — a quasi-irreversible, leaky, compartment-restricted modality, not a clean irreversible acrylamide-type warhead. Related cysteines (C110, C178) are redox/nitrosylation-sensitive regulatory sites, reinforcing that IDE's cysteines are redox handles rather than robust covalent drug anchors. Selective, durable covalent inhibition via Cys819 is mechanistically marginal.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: No credible covalent BIC thesis. (1) Target is unvalidated — zero approved or clinical drugs after six decades, so there is no clinical proof a covalent SM could 'beat.' (2) Covalent space is not open — Cys819 covalent inhibitors are already published (ACS Chem Biol 2015), undermining the patent-radar 'no covalent program' flag. (3) Mechanistically poor — the targetable cysteine is non-catalytic and the only demonstrated covalent chemistry is a reducible disulfide limited to extracellular enzyme, not a durable irreversible bond. (4) Broken/contradictory biology — diabetes wants IDE inhibition but catalytic inhibition (BDM44768) actually IMPAIRED glucose tolerance in mice; Alzheimer's wants the OPPOSITE (IDE activation to clear Abeta); IDE pleiotropy (insulin, glucagon, amylin, Abeta, ANP) makes a clean covalent-inhibition therapeutic hypothesis untenable. None of the standard covalent advantages (selectivity, duration, resistance, oral durability) translate into a winning story here.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No approved selective PKCalpha small molecule exists for a PRKCA-driven indication. (1) Aprinocarsen (ISIS 3521/LY900003) - the one agent directly targeting PRKCA - was an ANTISENSE OLIGONUCLEOTIDE (biologic-class, not a small molecule) that FAILED Phase III in NSCLC and was discontinued in 2005. (2) Midostaurin (approved) is a multi-kinase inhibitor approved for FLT3-mutant AML on its FLT3 activity, not PKCalpha. Enzastaurin (PKCbeta-preferring) failed Phase III in glioblastoma/DLBCL; sotrastaurin discontinued. (3) Darovasertib (LXS196) is the modern targeted PKC small molecule, but it is a PAN-PKC inhibitor in uveal melanoma where the driver is GNAQ/GNA11 upstream of PKC - it validates the PKC pathway in a Gq-driven setting, not PRKCA as a standalone target. Net: validation is weak, indirect, and dominated by a failed antisense agent plus pathway-level (not PRKCA-specific) drugs.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. No covalent small-molecule PKCalpha program or drug surfaced in searches ("PRKCA covalent inhibitor", company/biotech covalent PKCalpha 2023-2025) - consistent with the patent radar. The field has covalent kinase inhibitors broadly (ibrutinib, osimertinib, etc.) but PKCalpha is not among them and is not listed among the ~11 human kinases with a targetable front-pocket N-cap ATP-site cysteine.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/unfavorable. No documented reactive ATP-site or front-pocket N-cap cysteine for PKCalpha (it is not among the front-pocket-cysteine kinome). The well-characterized reactive cysteines (e.g., Cys151) sit in the C1 REGULATORY zinc-finger domain - redox-sensitive, Zn-coordinating thiols, not catalytic. These C1 cysteine motifs are highly conserved across ALL conventional and novel PKC isoforms and across the broader C1-domain proteome, so covalently targeting them would be a selectivity liability, not an asset. The single CysDB-ligandable cysteine does not map to a catalytic or selectively addressable allosteric site that would confer isoform-selective inhibition.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: No viable covalent BIC thesis. The decisive problem is target biology direction: the Newton lab (Cell 2015) established that PKCalpha / conventional PKCs are predominantly TUMOR SUPPRESSORS in cancer - most cancer-associated mutations are loss-of-function, and this explains the near-uniform failure of PKC inhibitors in oncology trials. Inhibiting a tumor suppressor is the wrong direction. The rare oncogenic allele (chordoid glioma PRKCA D463H) is a kinase-INACTIVE gain-of-function acting via protein-protein interactions, so an ATP-competitive covalent inhibitor cannot address it. There is no catalytic-site cysteine for a selective, durable covalent inhibitor, and the only reactive cysteines lie in a pan-PKC-conserved regulatory zinc finger (selectivity killer). The empty patent/covalent field reflects absence of a credible thesis, not an overlooked opening. A covalent small molecule offers no differentiated path over the failed inhibitor history here.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No drug directly targets NFKB1/p50 itself; it is validated only INDIRECTLY at the pathway level. Approved proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib, carfilzomib, ixazomib; multiple myeloma, MCL, Waldenstrom) suppress NF-kB activity but are pleiotropic cytotoxic agents, not p50-selective. IKK/IKKbeta inhibitors (PS-1145, BMS-345541, BAY 65-5811, SPC-839, etc.) reached early clinical/preclinical testing but none became a useful drug due to pathway-wide, on-mechanism toxicity. Modality of validation is therefore weak: broad cytotoxic/pathway agents, NOT a modern p50-selective targeted small molecule and NOT a biologic against NFKB1. NFKB1 itself is a transcription factor long regarded as 'undruggable'.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: A covalent precedent ALREADY EXISTS on the exact ligandable cysteine. The natural product andrographolide (alpha,beta-unsaturated butyrolactone) covalently modifies reduced Cys62 of p50 via Michael addition, blocking NF-kB DNA binding (Xia et al., J Immunol 2004, PMID 15356172; mechanism/SAR in J Nat Prod 2014). Andrographolide and its derivatives are studied anti-inflammatory/anti-cancer agents and andrographolide is a marketed herbal medicine in China. Endogenous covalent/redox modifiers of the same Cys62 (S-glutathionylation, S-nitrosylation, sulfenylation) are also documented. No modern, rationally designed, p50-SELECTIVE covalent drug-development program or clinical candidate was found in web search (2023-2025) — so the 'designed drug' space is unoccupied, but the cysteine is NOT chemically virgin: a promiscuous covalent chemotype already hits it.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Cys62 is a genuinely functional, mechanistically attractive cysteine. It sits in the DNA-binding/dimerization domain of p50; its reduced thiol is REQUIRED for kappaB-site DNA binding, and covalent or redox modification (glutathionylation, NO, oxidation, andrographolide adduct) abolishes DNA binding (C62S mutant is insensitive). So covalent engagement directly disables the protein's function — this is the strong part of the case. The fatal weakness is SELECTIVITY: Cys62 is conserved across the Rel/NF-kB family (the RHR/RxxRxR motif region), so a Cys62 warhead risks cross-reacting with RelA/p65, p52, RelB, c-Rel. Andrographolide's known promiscuity across NF-kB subunits and other targets illustrates exactly this liability. Functional cysteine: yes. Selectively druggable cysteine: unproven and high-risk.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: Thin. The attractive piece is a real functional Cys62 whose covalent engagement blocks p50 DNA binding, and the absence of a modern designed covalent program leaves nominal white space. But three things gut the BIC case: (1) validation is indirect and old-school — pleiotropic proteasome/IKK agents, with a long graveyard of failed direct NF-kB inhibitors driven by ubiquitous, pleiotropic NF-kB biology (broad immunosuppression/toxicity is the core reason this target class has repeatedly failed in clinic); (2) a covalent chemotype (andrographolide) already labels the exact Cys62 and is even a marketed natural product, so the cysteine is not virgin and the differentiation story ('first covalent') is weakened; (3) Cys62 is conserved across the Rel family, making subunit-selective covalent inhibition the central, unsolved technical risk. A covalent small molecule could in principle deliver oral, durable p50-selective blockade that biologics/PROTAC-free approaches cannot — but only if selectivity over other Rel subunits and a tolerability window against pleiotropic NF-kB toxicity are solved, neither of which has precedent. This is a high-risk discovery bet, not a clean BIC lane.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No approved or clinical drug selectively targets BMPR1A (ALK3). "Validation" is weak and indirect: (a) human genetics — germline LOSS-of-function mutations cause juvenile polyposis syndrome and Cowden/Bannayan-Riley-Ruvalcaba (classic Knudson two-hit tumor suppressor); (b) only non-selective tool compounds exist (dorsomorphin, LDN-193189, DMH1, LDN-212854, K02288) — all pan-BMP type-I inhibitors, never approved, limited by toxicity. Where BMP type-I inhibition is genuinely drugged clinically (anemia of inflammation/hepcidin; FOP), the lead receptor is ALK2/ACVR1, not ALK3 (e.g., zilurgisertib/INCB00928, BCX9250 — all non-covalent ALK2 programs). Modality of any real validation: tool compounds / genetics only, not a marketed targeted small molecule or biologic against BMPR1A itself.
deep_verdicts.existing_covalent: None found. No covalent small-molecule program or drug against BMPR1A/ALK3 in literature or web search; patent radar shows no covalent program. All reported ALK3-active chemotypes (dorsomorphin/LDN/DMH/K02288 series) are reversible, ATP-competitive, type-I inhibitors. However, "open" is moot here — the target is not desirable to inhibit.
deep_verdicts.cysteine_rationale: Weak/unsupported. The 1 CysDB hit is not annotated as a catalytic or functionally validated allosteric cysteine for ALK3. The druggable pocket is the ATP site (~residues 240-248), engaged only by reversible type-I inhibitors; no covalent-handle cysteine (e.g., front-pocket/DFG-adjacent) is described that would confer selectivity. Critically, the ALK1/2/3/6 kinase domains are highly homologous, so even reversible selectivity is hard and a covalent warhead would not obviously resolve it — selectivity case is unproven.
deep_verdicts.bic_thesis: No viable covalent BIC thesis. The fatal flaw is directionality: BMPR1A is a TUMOR SUPPRESSOR — disease is caused by loss of signaling, so oncology wants to RESTORE/activate BMPR1A, not inhibit it. A covalent inhibitor would phenocopy the disease-causing LOF mutation, and chronic ALK3 inhibition is expected to impair intestinal crypt stem-cell turnover (the juvenile-polyposis mechanism), creating intrinsic on-target GI toxicity. The only contexts that want BMP type-I inhibition (anemia of inflammation, FOP) are led by ALK2, where non-covalent inhibitors already work and adding a covalent warhead offers no clear selectivity, oral, or resistance advantage. Net: validated as a gene, but validated in the WRONG direction for an inhibitor, plus an unproven cysteine and a severe paralog-selectivity problem.

deep_verdicts.validating_drugs: No FDA-approved drug validates SOAT1 directly; clinical validation is WEAK and largely historical. Avasimibe (CI-1011), the most advanced ACAT/SOAT1 inhibitor, was terminated in Phase 3 for atherosclerosis (neutral/negative IVUS outcome plus CYP3A4 induction that blunted background statins). Nevanimibe/ATR-101 (adrenal-selective SOAT1 inhibitor) ran a Phase 1 in metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) with ZERO complete/partial responses and only ~27% stable disease - disappointing. Other clinical-stage ACAT/SOAT1 inhibitors (F12511/eflucimibe, K-604, pactimibe/CS-505) never reached approval. Indirect validation: mitotane (approved adrenolytic for ACC) partially acts via SOAT1 inhibition (free-cholesterol/ER-stress-driven apoptosis), and SOAT1 expression correlates with poor prognosis across HCC, ACC, prostate, glioma, pancreatic cancers.
